title: Find heat islands and at-risk populations in Madison, Wisconsin
method: Interpolate 139 station temperatures (TemperatureF, EPSG:6610) to a continuous surface with ordinary Kriging, average the surface within each of the 269 census block groups, map the block-group means as a choropleth and outline block groups that are both hot and dense in people aged 65+.
benchmark_defects: The published reference script uses pykrige for Kriging; the checks accept any Kriging implementation (pykrige, gstools, a Gaussian-process regressor or a hand-written kriging system).
checks: required: per-block-group mean temperature (table, Series or 269-value array) rank-correlates with gold block means (Spearman >= 0.90)
required: values are temperatures of this data set (mean within 2 F of gold)
required: block values come from a surface (< 50 % equal a station reading)
required: the drawn choropleth colour values are the per-block temperature (rho >= 0.90)
required: hot & elderly-dense highlight subset derived (1-60 % of blocks, mean temp and density percentile > 0.6; code-line evidence for inline selections)
required: the prescribed method was used - pykrige OK/UK, gstools kriging, a GP regressor or a hand-written kriging system in the code
